= BITwiki Ontology Index: Living Reference for Knowledge Structure =

== Etymology: The Study of Being ==

''Ontology'' — from Greek ''ontos'' (being, present participle of ''einai'', to be) + ''logia'' (study of, from ''legein'', to speak). The study of being, of what exists, of the nature of existence itself.

But what if existence is not static? What if being is becoming? This index treats ontology not as a fixed catalog of categories but as a living substrate—an evolving field of distinctions that emerge from use, stabilize through validation, and dissolve when no longer serviceable.

== Purpose: Why Structure Matters ==

This document serves as a reference point for BITwiki's ontology. It offers:
* '''Orientation''': Ways to navigate the knowledge field
* '''Vocabulary''': Shared language for describing entities
* '''Patterns''': Recurring structures that facilitate query and discovery
* '''Extension points''': Places where new distinctions can emerge

It does not prescribe. It describes what has stabilized. It marks what remains provisional. It leaves space for what has not yet emerged.

== Ontology Overview: An Evolving Field ==

BITwiki's ontology consists of:
* '''Canonical Entity Types''': Core categories that have achieved stability through use
* '''Extended Entity Types''': Additional categories that serve specific domains
* '''Core Properties''': Attributes that describe entities across types
* '''Relationship Types''': Connections that weave entities into webs of meaning

These are not fixed. They are sedimentations—temporary stabilizations from the flow of knowledge-making.

== Entity Types: Modes of Crystallization ==

=== Canonical Types ===

These types have achieved stability through extensive use and cross-domain validation:

| Type | Description | Example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| Topic | A subject domain or field of knowledge | Systems Science |
| Idea | An abstract concept or theoretical construct | Feedback Loop |
| Implementation | A concrete realization of an idea | Thermostat |
| Project | An organized effort with defined goals | BITwiki Development |
| Protocol | A prescribed procedure or set of rules | Validation Protocol |
| Dataset | A structured collection of data | GenBank |

'''Note''': These types emerged from use. They are not final. New types may crystallize; existing types may dissolve or transform.

'''Details''': [[BITwiki Page Types]]

=== Extended Types ===

These types serve specific domains and may achieve pattern stability through validation:

| Type | Description | Example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| Person | Individual human agent | Norbert Wiener |
| Organization | Structured group of agents | MIT |
| Event | Time-bounded occurrence | Macy Conferences |
| Publication | Documented work | Cybernetics (1948) |
| Location | Physical or virtual place | Cambridge, MA |
| Technology | Tool or system | Semantic MediaWiki |

'''Details''': [[BITwiki Expanded Entity Types]]

== Core Properties: Dimensions of Description ==

Properties are not final. They emerge from the need to describe, to differentiate, to query. The following properties have achieved stability:

=== Identification ===

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| Has entity type | Page | Classification into entity types |
| Has name | Text | Human-readable identifier |
| Has description | Text | Brief characterization |

=== Epistemic ===

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| Has epistemic status | Text | Validation tier (Hypothetical/Emerging/Established/Verified/Axiomatic) |
| Has confidence | Text | Qualitative certainty assessment |
| Has source count | Number | Distribution of validation sources |

=== Provenance ===

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| Has originator | Page | Initial crystallization agent |
| Has date | Date | Moment of emergence |
| Has source | URL | External validation trajectory |

=== Workflow ===

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| Has workflow state | Text | Current phase (Draft/Beta/Stable) |
| Has version | Text | Version identifier |
| Has validator | Page | Validation agent |

'''Details''': [[Property Types]]

== Relationship Types: Webs of Connection ==

Relationships are paths through the knowledge field. They describe how entities influence, contain, depend upon, and validate each other.

=== Structural ===

| Relationship | From | To | Example |
|--------------|------|-----|-----------|
| Is a | Entity | Type | Feedback Loop is a Idea |
| Part of | Part | Whole | Wheel part of Car |
| Contains | Whole | Part | Car contains Wheel |

=== Causal ===

| Relationship | From | To | Example |
|--------------|------|-----|-----------|
| Causes | Cause | Effect | Stress causes Cortisol |
| Depends on | Dependent | Dependency | App depends on Framework |
| Enables | Enabler | Enabled | SMW enables Queries |

=== Epistemic ===

| Relationship | From | To | Example |
|--------------|------|-----|-----------|
| Supported by | Claim | Evidence | Theory supported by Data |
| Contradicts | Claim | Claim | A contradicts B |
| Implements | Concrete | Abstract | Thermostat implements Feedback |

'''Details''': [[BITwiki Semantic Patterns]]

== SMW Queries: Patterns of Discovery ==

=== Entity Queries ===

'''All Ideas:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]}}
```

'''Established Ideas:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has epistemic status::Established]]
}}
```

'''Verified Claims:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has epistemic status::Verified]]}}
```

=== Property Queries ===

'''All properties:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has type::+]]}}
```

'''Numeric properties:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has type::Number]]}}
```

=== Relationship Queries ===

'''What implements Feedback Loop:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Implements::Feedback Loop]]}}
```

'''What depends on X:'''
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Depends on::X]]}}
```

== Ontology Principles: Guidelines, Not Rules ==

=== 1. Machine Readability ===

Content should be machine-readable where possible:
* Typed properties enable queries
* Structured data facilitates export
* Semantic markup supports discovery

But readability serves human understanding. Never sacrifice clarity for structure.

=== 2. Human Legibility ===

Content should be human-legible:
* Clear labels reduce cognitive load
* Accessible language invites participation
* Progressive disclosure respects attention
* Visual hierarchy guides navigation

=== 3. Extensibility ===

Ontology should accommodate growth:
* New types can emerge from use
* New properties can be defined
* Relationships can be customized
* Queries can be adapted

Extension is not failure of foresight. It is recognition that knowledge evolves.

=== 4. Validation ===

Ontology should be validated:
* Property types can be checked
* Constraints can be enforced
* Consistency can be verified
* Errors can be flagged

Validation is service, not constraint. It helps maintain coherence without preventing innovation.

# Property Types. (2026). SMW property reference.
# BITwiki Semantic Patterns. (2026). Relationship documentation.

# W3C. (2014). RDF Schema 1.1.
# OWL 2 Web Ontology Language. (2012).
# Gruber, T.R. (1993). A translation approach to portable ontology specifications.
# Smith, B. (2003). Ontology.
# BITwiki Constitution. (2026). Foundational principles.

= BITwiki Ontology Index: Comprehensive Entity Type Reference =

== Etymology: The Study of Being ==

''Ontology'' — from Greek ''ontos'' (being, present participle of ''einai'', to be) + ''logia'' (study of, from ''legein'', to speak). The study of being, of what exists, of the nature of existence itself.

But what if existence is not static? What if being is becoming? This index treats ontology not as a fixed catalog of categories but as a living substrate—an evolving field of distinctions that emerge from use, stabilize through validation, and dissolve when no longer serviceable.

== Purpose: Why Structure Matters ==

This document serves as the central reference for BITwiki's ontology. It offers:
* '''Orientation''': Ways to navigate the knowledge field
* '''Vocabulary''': Shared language for describing entities
* '''Patterns''': Recurring structures that facilitate query and discovery
* '''Extension points''': Places where new distinctions can emerge

It does not prescribe. It describes what has stabilized. It marks what remains provisional. It leaves space for what has not yet emerged.

== What This System Does ==

BITwiki organizes knowledge through explicit semantic relationships rather than implicit categories. Where traditional encyclopedias bury connections in prose, BITwiki surfaces them as queryable data.

Consider the difference: Wikipedia's article on "Cybernetics" mentions Norbert Wiener in passing. BITwiki encodes `[[Has originator::Norbert Wiener]]` as machine-readable data, enabling queries like "All ideas originated by MIT researchers between 1940-1960."

== Overview ==

BITwiki's ontology provides the structural foundation for its recursive knowledge system. Unlike traditional encyclopedias that rely on implicit categories, BITwiki makes ontological commitments explicit through six canonical entity types, extended types for specialized domains, and machine-queryable relationships via Semantic MediaWiki.

This document serves as the definitive reference for entity types, their properties, validation rules, and SMW implementation.

== Ontology Overview: An Evolving Field ==

BITwiki's ontology consists of:
* '''Canonical Entity Types''': Core categories that have achieved stability through use
* '''Extended Entity Types''': Additional categories that serve specific domains
* '''Core Properties''': Attributes that describe entities across types
* '''Relationship Types''': Connections that weave entities into webs of meaning

These are not fixed. They are sedimentations—temporary stabilizations from the flow of knowledge-making.

== 1. Six Canonical Entity Types ==

BITwiki recognizes six fundamental entity types that cover the full spectrum of knowledge artifacts:

=== 1.1 Topic ===

'''Etymology:''' From Greek ''topos''—place, location, later a domain of inquiry.

'''Definition:''' Subject matter domains with hierarchical and lateral relationships.

'''Purpose:''' Topics provide the organizational backbone of BITwiki, enabling navigation from general domains to specific subjects.

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has subtopic::Topic]] — Narrower subject domains
* [[Has related topic::Topic]] — Lateral associations
* [[Has domain boundary::Description]] — Scope delimitation
* [[Has prerequisite topic::Topic]] — Knowledge dependencies
* [[Has application domain::Domain]] — Where this topic applies

'''Examples:'''
* Systems Science (root topic)
* Cybernetics (subtopic of Systems Science)
* Control Theory (subtopic of Cybernetics)
* PID Controllers (implementation within Control Theory)

'''Validation Rules:'''
* Must have at least one parent topic or be declared as root
* Must have at least three related entities (topics, ideas, or implementations)
* Must have explicit domain boundaries
* Must not be redundant with existing topics

'''SMW Implementation:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Topic]]
[[Has subtopic::Cybernetics]]
[[Has related topic::Information Theory]]
[[Has domain boundary::Study of systems and their interactions]]
```

'''Epistemic Status:''' Topics are typically Established or Verified (they exist as recognized domains of study).

=== 1.2 Idea ===

'''Etymology:''' From Greek ''idein''—to see, later a mental conception or thought.

'''Definition:''' Abstract concepts, theories, frameworks, and mental models.

'''Purpose:''' Ideas capture the conceptual content of knowledge—hypotheses, theories, principles, and frameworks.

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has originator::Person]] — Who first proposed this idea
* [[Has development history::Description]] — Evolution of the concept
* [[Has criticism::Idea]] — Counter-arguments and limitations
* [[Has refinement::Idea]] — Later developments and improvements
* [[Has application::Implementation]] — Concrete realizations
* [[Has related idea::Idea]] — Conceptual neighbors
* [[Has epistemic foundation::Source]] — Evidentiary basis

'''Examples:'''
* Emergence (systems theory concept)
* Feedback loops (cybernetics concept)
* Recursion (computation/mathematics concept)
* Toroidal structures (geometry/systems concept)

'''Validation Rules:'''
* Must have historical trace (originator or first appearance)
* Must have contemporary relevance (cited in recent sources)
* Must distinguish from similar ideas (disambiguation)
* Must include criticism or limitations (no idea is perfect)

'''SMW Implementation:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has originator::Ludwig von Bertalanffy]]
[[Has development history::General systems theory (1968) → Complex systems (1980s) → Complexity science (2000s)]]
[[Has criticism::Reductionist critique: emergence is epiphenomenal]]
[[Has application::Neural networks, ecosystems, economies]]
```

'''Epistemic Status:''' Ideas span all tiers from Hypothetical (new conjectures) to Verified (well-established theories).

=== 1.3 Implementation ===

'''Etymology:''' From Latin ''implementum''—filling up, from ''implere'' (to fill, complete).

'''Definition:''' Concrete realizations of ideas in technology, method, or practice.

'''Purpose:''' Implementations bridge abstract ideas and practical application, enabling assessment of ideas through their effects.

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has specification::Description]] — Technical details
* [[Has performance metric::Metric]] — How success is measured
* [[Has limitation::Description]] — Constraints and failure modes
* [[Has successor::Implementation]] — Later versions or replacements
* [[Has predecessor::Implementation]] — Earlier versions
* [[Has component::Implementation]] — Subsystems
* [[Has requirement::Requirement]] — Necessary conditions
* [[Has standard::Standard]] — Compliance specifications

'''Examples:'''
* PID controllers (implementation of control theory)
* Neural networks (implementation of connectionism)
* Semantic MediaWiki (implementation of semantic web ideas)
* Blockchain (implementation of distributed trust)

'''Validation Rules:'''
* Must have operational definition (what does it do?)
* Must have empirical assessment (does it work?)
* Must document limitations (when does it fail?)
* Must trace to originating idea(s)

'''SMW Implementation:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Implementation]]
[[Has specification::Proportional-Integral-Derivative control algorithm]]
[[Has performance metric::Settling time, overshoot, steady-state error]]
[[Has limitation::Nonlinear systems, time delays, sensor noise]]
[[Has predecessor::On-off control]]
[[Has component::Proportional term, Integral term, Derivative term]]
```

'''Epistemic Status:''' Implementations are typically Established or Verified (they exist and function).

=== 1.4 Project ===

'''Etymology:''' From Latin ''proiectum''—something thrown forth, from ''proicere'' (to throw forward).

'''Definition:''' Organized efforts with goals, timelines, and outcomes.

'''Purpose:''' Projects capture the social and organizational dimension of knowledge creation and application.

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has goal::Description]] — What the project aims to achieve
* [[Has timeline::Date range]] — Duration and milestones
* [[Has outcome::Result]] — What was achieved
* [[Has participant::Person/Organization]] — Who was involved
* [[Has resource::Resource]] — What was required
* [[Has sponsor::Organization]] — Funding or support
* [[Has deliverable::Artifact]] — Tangible outputs
* [[Has impact::Impact]] — Effects on knowledge or practice

'''Examples:'''
* BITwiki (knowledge system project)
* Human Genome Project (scientific project)
* Apollo Program (engineering project)
* Manhattan Project (historical project)

'''Validation Rules:'''
* Must have documented initiation (when did it start?)
* Must have assessment (success, failure, or ongoing)
* Must include participant attribution
* Must trace to ideas and implementations

'''SMW Implementation:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Project]]
[[Has goal::Sequence the human genome]]
[[Has timeline::1990-2003]]
[[Has outcome::Complete genome sequence published 2003]]
[[Has participant::International consortium of 20 institutions]]
[[Has resource::$3 billion USD, 200+ researchers]]
[[Has impact::Enabled personalized medicine, ancestry testing]]
```

'''Epistemic Status:''' Projects are typically Established or Verified (they happened and have outcomes).

=== 1.5 Protocol ===

'''Etymology:''' From Greek ''protokollon''—first sheet glued to manuscript, from ''protos'' (first) + ''kolla'' (glue).

'''Definition:''' Prescribed procedures for knowledge generation, validation, or governance.

'''Purpose:''' Protocols ensure reproducibility, quality, and consistency in knowledge work.

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has step::Step]] — Ordered procedure components
* [[Has prerequisite::Condition]] — Requirements before starting
* [[Has success criterion::Criterion]] — How to know it worked
* [[Has failure mode::Description]] — How it can go wrong
* [[Has validation method::Method]] — How to verify correctness
* [[Has scope::Description]] — When to apply this protocol
* [[Has authority::Source]] — Who established this protocol
* [[Has variant::Protocol]] — Alternative versions

'''Examples:'''
* Scientific method (knowledge generation protocol)
* Peer review (validation protocol)
* Epistemic upgrade protocol (governance protocol)
* Recursive validation (BITwiki-specific protocol)

'''Validation Rules:'''
* Must be reproducible (others can follow it)
* Must have effectiveness assessment (does it achieve its goal?)
* Must document failure modes (when does it fail?)
* Must have scope limitations (when not to use it)

'''SMW Implementation:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Protocol]]
[[Has step::Observation → Hypothesis → Prediction → Experiment → Analysis]]
[[Has prerequisite::Testable hypothesis, measurable variables]]
[[Has success criterion::Reproducible results, falsifiable predictions]]
[[Has failure mode::Confirmation bias, p-hacking, irreproducibility]]
[[Has authority::Philosophy of science community]]
```

'''Epistemic Status:''' Protocols are typically Verified (they work) or Axiomatic (they define how BITwiki operates).

=== 1.6 Dataset ===

'''Etymology:''' From Latin ''dare''—to give, later a collection of facts or information.

'''Definition:''' Collections of structured data with provenance and licensing.

'''Purpose:''' Datasets provide the evidentiary foundation for claims and enable reproducible analysis.

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has size::Quantity]] — Magnitude (records, bytes)
* [[Has format::Format]] — File format or schema
* [[Has source::Source]] — Origin and collection method
* [[Has license::License]] — Usage rights
* [[Has quality metric::Metric]] — Completeness, accuracy, bias
* [[Has temporal coverage::Date range]] — Time period covered
* [[Has spatial coverage::Location]] — Geographic scope
* [[Has variable::Variable]] — What the data measures
* [[Has access method::Method]] — How to obtain the data

'''Examples:'''
* Wikipedia corpus (text dataset)
* GenBank (genetic sequence dataset)
* Climate data (temperature, precipitation records)
* BITwiki itself (knowledge graph dataset)

'''Validation Rules:'''
* Must be accessible (or have access method)
* Must have documentation (what do the data mean?)
* Must have quality assessment (how good are the data?)
* Must have provenance (where did it come from?)

'''SMW Implementation:'''
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Dataset]]
[[Has size::6.5 million articles, 100+ GB]]
[[Has format::XML dump, SQL database]]
[[Has source::Wikimedia Foundation]]
[[Has license::CC-BY-SA 4.0]]
[[Has quality metric::Editorial review, citation requirements]]
[[Has temporal coverage::2001-present]]
[[Has variable::Article text, edit history, user contributions]]
```

'''Epistemic Status:''' Datasets are typically Verified (they exist and are used) or Axiomatic (BITwiki's own data).

== 2. Extended Entity Types ==

Beyond the six canonical types, BITwiki supports extended types for specialized domains:

=== 2.1 Person ===

'''Definition:''' Individual contributors with expertise and contributions.

'''Extends:''' Idea (originator), Project (participant), Implementation (developer)

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has expertise::Topic]] — Areas of knowledge
* [[Has contribution::Entity]] — What they created or influenced
* [[Has affiliation::Organization]] — Institutional connections
* [[Has credential::Credential]] — Qualifications (not required)

'''Examples:'''
* Ludwig von Bertalanffy (systems theory)
* Norbert Wiener (cybernetics)
* Claude Shannon (information theory)

=== 2.2 Organization ===

'''Definition:''' Institutions, companies, collectives.

'''Extends:''' Project (sponsor), Dataset (source), Implementation (developer)

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has member::Person]] — Individuals involved
* [[Has output::Entity]] — What the organization produces
* [[Has mission::Description]] — Purpose and goals

'''Examples:'''
* Santa Fe Institute (complexity research)
* Wikimedia Foundation (knowledge infrastructure)
* BITCORE (BITwiki development)

=== 2.3 Event ===

'''Definition:''' Historical occurrences with temporal boundaries.

'''Extends:''' Project (milestone), Idea (origin), Implementation (deployment)

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has date::Date]] — When it occurred
* [[Has location::Location]] — Where it occurred
* [[Has participant::Person/Organization]] — Who was involved
* [[Has outcome::Result]] — What happened

'''Examples:'''
* Macy Conferences (cybernetics history)
* Launch of Wikipedia (2001)
* First human genome sequence (2003)

=== 2.4 Publication ===

'''Definition:''' Books, articles, documents with citation data.

'''Extends:''' Dataset (source), Idea (vehicle), Protocol (documentation)

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has author::Person]] — Who wrote it
* [[Has date::Date]] — When published
* [[Has venue::Source]] — Where published
* [[Has citation count::Number]] — Impact metric

'''Examples:'''
* "General System Theory" (Bertalanffy, 1968)
* "Cybernetics" (Wiener, 1948)
* "A Mathematical Theory of Communication" (Shannon, 1948)

=== 2.5 Tool ===

'''Definition:''' Instruments, software, methodologies.

'''Extends:''' Implementation (instrument), Protocol (methodology)

'''Properties:'''
* [[Has function::Description]] — What it does
* [[Has input::Description]] — What it requires
* [[Has output::Description]] — What it produces

'''Examples:'''
* SMW (knowledge representation tool)
* Python (programming tool)
* Jupyter notebooks (analysis tool)

== 3. Relationship Patterns ==

=== 3.1 Hierarchical Relationships ===

'''Is a (subclass):''' [[Is a::Entity type]] — Type membership
'''Has subclass:''' Inverse of Is a
'''Has part:''' [[Has part::Entity]] — Component relationship
'''Is part of:''' Inverse of Has part

=== 3.2 Lateral Relationships ===

'''Related to:''' [[Related to::Entity]] — Association without hierarchy
'''Depends on:''' [[Depends on::Entity]] — Dependency
'''Validates:''' [[Validates::Claim]] — Evidence relationship
'''Conflicts with:''' [[Conflicts with::Entity]] — Opposition

=== 3.3 Temporal Relationships ===

'''Precedes:''' [[Precedes::Entity]] — Temporal order
'''Succeeds:''' Inverse of Precedes
'''Enables:''' [[Enables::Entity]] — Causal facilitation
'''Inhibits:''' [[Inhibits::Entity]] — Causal obstruction

=== 3.4 Epistemic Relationships ===

'''Has evidence:''' [[Has evidence::Source]] — Support
'''Has counter-evidence:''' [[Has counter-evidence::Source]] — Opposition
'''Has confidence:''' [[Has confidence score::Number]] — Quantified certainty
'''Has status:''' [[Has epistemic status::Status]] — Tier assignment

== 4. SMW Query Patterns ==

=== 4.1 Entity Type Queries ===

All Topics:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Topic]]
|?Has subtopic
|?Has related topic
|format=table
}}
```

All Verified Ideas:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]] [[Has epistemic status::Verified]]
|?Has originator
|?Has confidence score
|format=table
}}
```

=== 4.2 Relationship Queries ===

What validates a claim:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Validates::{{PAGENAME}}]]
|?Has confidence score
|format=ul
}}
```

What depends on this:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Depends on::{{PAGENAME}}]]
|format=ul
}}
```

=== 4.3 Epistemic Queries ===

High-confidence claims:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has confidence score::>0.8]]
|?Has epistemic status
|?Has confidence score
|sort=Has confidence score
|order=desc
}}
```

All Established entities:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has epistemic status::Established]]}}
```

== 5. Validation and Quality ==

=== 5.1 Ontology Validation Rules ===

# '''Type Consistency:''' Every page must have exactly one canonical entity type
# '''Property Completeness:''' Required properties must be present
# '''Relationship Integrity:''' Referenced entities must exist
# '''Epistemic Marking:''' Every claim must have status and confidence
# '''Provenance:''' Every entity must have source attribution

=== 5.2 Quality Metrics ===
* '''Coverage:''' Percentage of pages with complete ontological markup
* '''Consistency:''' Ratio of valid relationships to total relationships
* '''Connectivity:''' Average path length between related entities
* '''Depth:''' Hierarchical depth of topic trees

== Epistemic Integration ==

Every entity carries epistemic metadata:
* '''Status''': Hypothetical → Emerging → Established → Verified → Deprecated
* '''Confidence''': 0.0-1.0 score with justification
* '''Provenance''': Origin, transmission, current state

This enables queries like "All claims with confidence >0.8 from the last decade" or "All deprecated ideas and their replacements."

== On the Nature of This Framework ==

This ontology is not a discovery but a construction—tools forged for a purpose. The types and relationships described here emerged from practice, not imposed from theory. They are subject to revision, expansion, and retirement as our understanding evolves.

The guiding question is always: ''Does this enhance our substrate or limit it?''
